ui_bugs.issue: copyText() uses a sync try/catch around navigator.clipboard.writeText(), which returns a Promise. When clipboard permission is denied (or in non-secure contexts), the Promise rejection is unhandled and surfaces as 'Uncaught runtime error: Failed to execute writeText on Clipboard: Write permission denied' — triggers the webpack dev overlay and can block subsequent clicks. In real users with clipboard permission the toast fires correctly, so user impact is low, but the error should be caught. Fix: make copyText async and await + .catch the writeText promise, or use navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(...).catch(fallback).

action_items: (Optional/low priority) Harden copyText in ExtraDialogs.jsx & SpecialDialogs.jsx: await navigator.clipboard.writeText and catch the async rejection so it doesn't surface as an uncaught runtime error when clipboard permission is denied.
critical_code_review_comments: copyText helper in ExtraDialogs.jsx (line 10-15) and likely mirrored in SpecialDialogs.jsx does not await the Promise returned by clipboard.writeText; sync try/catch cannot catch async rejections. Recommend: async function copyText(t){ try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(t); return true; } catch { return false; } } — and await it in share().

rca of the issue: Share button unhandled rejection: navigator.clipboard.writeText is Promise-based; the copyText wrapper's synchronous try/catch cannot capture the async rejection. In Playwright headless (permission denied) this bubbles to window.onerror and triggers the webpack-dev-server overlay iframe that then intercepts pointer events on the page. Repro: revoke clipboard permission, click Share — see runtime error. Mitigation: await the Promise and catch in async function, or attach .catch().
